title: Knuckle cracking = arthritis? He tested it 60 years 🖐️
description:
Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis? Dr Donald Unger cracked the knuckles of his left hand at least twice a day for more than 60 years, and never his right hand, as a control. By his estimate that's about 36,500 cracks. Result: no arthritis in either hand, and no difference between them (Arthritis & Rheumatism, 1998). It won him the 2009 Ig Nobel Prize in Medicine. A larger study that X-rayed the hands of 215 people found no link between habitual knuckle cracking and hand osteoarthritis (2011). The pop? Real-time MRI (2015) shows a gas cavity forming in the joint fluid as the joint surfaces separate; it takes about 20 minutes before that knuckle can crack again. (How the body works, not medical advice.)

Sources: Improbable Research (Ig Nobel 2009, Donald Unger); deWeber et al., J Am Board Fam Med 2011; Kawchuk et al., PLOS ONE 2015 (University of Alberta), via Science News and ScienceDaily.

meta.topic: the knuckle-cracking arthritis myth: Donald Unger cracked only his left hand's knuckles at least twice a day for 60+ years (~36,500 cracks), right hand as control; no arthritis in either hand (1998 letter, Ig Nobel 2009); 2011 study of 215 people X-rayed: no link; the pop = a gas cavity forming in the joint fluid (real-time MRI 2015); ~20 minutes to reset
meta.idea_source: viral-shaped + unique: a habit almost everyone has and a warning almost everyone has heard, busted by a real one-man 60-year experiment (a story few Shorts tell properly); backlog idea; body niche with a myth-bust after today's space what-if
